title: CRLR/528/2019 of BHARAT YADAV Vs NISHA YADAV

paras.text:
CRLR No.528 of 2019
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. S.K. Mandal, Advocate for the
revisionist.
Mr. P.S. Bohra, AGA for the State.
This is a criminal revision which has been
preferred by the revisionist, challenging the order
dated 14.09.2018, as passed by the learned Family
Court, District Udham Singh Nagar in Criminal
Case No. 158/2018, Smt. Nisha Yadav v. Bharat
Yadav, by virtue of the order impugned under
challenge, an application under sub Section (2) of
Section 125 of Cr.PC for the determination of
interim maintenance during the pendency of the
principal application under Section 125 of Cr.P.C.
has been granted by the learned Family Court, while
passing an order on an interim application paper No.
5 (ga), as well as on considering the objection
preferred by the revisionist i.e. paper No. 26 (ga).
It is reported by the Registry that the revision
has been preferred with a Delay Condonation
Application No. 2759/2019 with delay of 260 days.
Since this Court is not venturing into the
merits of the matter, because it is only an interim
arrangement made by the learned Family Court for
grant of maintenance @ of Rs. 4,000/- per month to
the respondent-wife, this Court is of the view that
while considering the delay condonation
application, and after hearing the counsel on the
same and after considering the medical report,
which has been submitted by him along with the
delay condonation application, showing his inability
to file the revision earlier because of an ailment,
which the revisionist was suffering from having
considered the documents and the reasons for the
delay, this Court is of the view that the delay
condonation application deserves to be allowed,
accordingly the delay of 260 days has been
satisfactorily explained and thus for the reasons
given therein which are satisfactory, the delay
condonation application is allowed, and the delay,
which has chanced in filing the revision is
condoned.

After having considered the propriety of the
order under challenge i.e. an order dated
09.09.2018, where the learned family Court has
directed to pay an interim maintenance of Rs.
4,000/- per month to the respondent-wife it is by
way of an interim measure only, that the Court has
taken into consideration the income which was
accruing to the revisionist-husband on account of
his engagement, which according to the respondent-wife was shown to be from agricultural activity,
which was being carried by him and also by running
a small dairy. However, this Court, at this stage, is
not determining the sanctity about the allegations of
the income accruing to the revisionist, but keeping
in mind that it is only an interim arrangement which
has been made during the pendency adjudication of
125 Application itself and the amount thus
determined to be paid by way of an interim
maintenance being Rs. 4,000/- per month only, this
Court is of the view that instead of keeping the
revision pending, it would in the interest of justice,
and for all the litigating parties too, that it may be
disposed of with a request to learned Family Court
to decide the application under Section 125 Cr.PC
as preferred by the respondent-wife itself within a
period of three months from today and for a period
of three months the maintenance as directed by the
learned Family Court would be continued to be paid
by the revisionist-husband to the respondent-wife.
However, it is made clear that, any
observations which has been made in the above part
of the order is not an expression given by this Court
on the merits of the matter.
Subject to above observation, the impugned
order is affirmed. Revision lacks merits and same is
accordingly dismissed.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
16.09.2019 Mahinder/
